mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points within one month signals monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to produce positive 20d returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion phases, high GDP growth (GDPC1) signals profit margin compression and rising interest rate expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods (defined by GDPC1 annualized growth above 2.5%), the S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) typically triggers monetary tightening expectations, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals an overheating labor market, prompting Fed rate hikes and economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE falls below 4.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, supporting corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST up and RSAFS up) fails to produce positive 20d returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In supply-constrained cycles (low industrial production growth), reduced corporate output and inflationary pressures lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In supply-constrained cycles (defined by INDPRO annualized growth below 0.5%), the S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
